blocks.content: NITI Aayog serves as the apex public policy think tank of the Government of India, promoting cooperative federalism.

rows: Allocated funds to state governments and central ministries
Purely an advisory think tank with no fund allocation powers
Limited to National Development Council interactions
Active participation of Chief Ministers in the Governing Council
Flexible structure with part-time members and domain experts

items: NITI Aayog is an extra-constitutional, non-statutory body created via a Cabinet resolution on January 1, 2015.
The Prime Minister serves as the ex-officio Chairperson, while the Chief Ministers of all states are members of the Governing Council.
Atal Innovation Mission is housed directly under NITI Aayog, not under the Ministry of Education or Ministry of Skill Development.
Unlike the former Planning Commission, NITI Aayog does not have financial powers to allocate funds to state governments.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) replaced the Planning Commission in 2015 to foster cooperative federalism.
Atal Innovation Mission (AIM) promotes innovation and entrepreneurship through Atal Tinkering Labs (ATLs) and Atal Incubation Centres (AICs).
Aspirational Districts Programme (ADP) aims to rapidly transform 112 under-developed districts through real-time tracking.
SATH (Sustainable Action for Transforming Human Capital) focuses on structural reforms in state health and education systems.
Key indices published include the SDG India Index, India Innovation Index, and Composite Water Management Index.
